description: Shared benchmark configuration. Read by every language harness so each one builds the byte-identical matrix and runs the same operations. See README for the generation scheme. Orientation is genes x cells (rows = genes, cols = cells): the huge dimension is cells (columns), which is the compressed axis for both scipy CSC and R SVT, so the left-multiply (vecmat) is each library's fast path and maps to a per-cell weighted sum of genes.

generation.comment: Deterministic modular map k_i = (i*stride) % (rows*cols), with row_i = k_i // cols, col_i = k_i % cols. 'stride' must be coprime to rows*cols (assert gcd==1 at startup) so the k_i are distinct -> no duplicate coordinates. Deterministic nonzero values: v_i = 1 + (k_i % value_mod). IMPORTANT: rows*cols, nnz, and all of k can exceed 2^31 (and may approach 2^53), so every harness MUST do this arithmetic in exact 64-bit integers -- Python ints are fine; R must use bit64::integer64 (NOT double, which silently loses precision past 2^53). rows*cols must stay below 2^63.

run.comment: Each operation is timed 'repetitions' times after 'warmup' untimed runs; report median + IQR downstream. CSC conversion (scipy) / SVT construction (R) is done once up front and is NOT timed. 'threads' is set to 1: the runner pins OMP/OPENBLAS/MKL threads for reproducibility and to make sure CPU time measures the true compute time. Both harnesses measure CPU time (user+system), which sums across threads, so it only equals true compute time when single-threaded.

output.comment: Tidy long-format CSV. Each script appends rows with these columns; merging is just concatenation. 'nnz' is written as an integer string to survive >2^31 values.
